subject: Private VPC observability onramp — collector/gateway connectivity checklist
messages:
From: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@globex.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: security-ops@globex.com
Date: 2028-09-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — Splunk HEC integration next steps

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Our security team needs a concrete checklist for network and auth so we can start a short POC in our staging VPC. Key asks from our side:
- Exact IP/port ranges for outbound connections (HEC, evidence upload)
- TLS mutual auth expectations (client certs vs mTLS termination)
- Expected token/key rotation cadence and vault options
- A minimal set of example events (log/trace) to validate forwarding mapping

Could you share a short runbook we can hand to infra and SecOps? Preferably with firewall snippets we can paste into our cloud firewall policy.

Best,
Alice
Alice Monroe
Sr. SecOps Engineer, Globex Corp

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@globex.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, Splunk Onboarding <onboard@splunk.com>
Date: 2028-09-16T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — Splunk HEC integration next steps

Alice — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a compact checklist & example snippets to speed runway. High-level answers here, details in the attachments and links:

1) Connectivity
- Outbound only from your on-prem / VPC egress: TCP 443 to our collector gateway endpoints (regional hostnames in the drive link).
- We recommend pinning to the regional FQDNs but allow the /24 range we list in the firewall template if you need numeric CIDRs.

2) TLS & auth
- Primary pattern: HTTPS + HEC token (bearer) with TLS server auth.
- For higher assurance we support mutual TLS at the gateway; we can flip on mTLS for your account. If you require mTLS, you will provision client certs, and we will provide the CA thumbprint for verification.

3) Key rotation
- HEC tokens are short-lived (rotatable on-demand). We recommend automated rotation every 90 days; if you need SOC-driven 30-day rotation we can support that as a managed service.

4) Example payloads
- See kp-siem-field-map-20280915.csv for minimal event samples and field mappings you can validate in Splunk.

Next steps I propose:
- Diego will share a minimal firewall snippet you can paste into your cloud rules.
- Marissa will produce the final HEC mapping we expect to land in Splunk (CSV).
- Once you confirm, we schedule a 60-min tunnel verification (light traffic) and an evidence bundle transfer.

Quick ask: can you confirm whether Globex wants mTLS or token-only for this POC? If mTLS, we need the CSR metadata by EOD Wednesday.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: kp-siem-field-map-20280915.csv (text/csv)]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Date: 2028-09-17T08:39:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — Splunk HEC integration next steps

Hi Alice — adding the mapping details and a short validation plan. Summary below and full attachment included.

Validation checklist (short):
1) Send a synthetic event with these three fields: timestamp, request_id, model_name.
2) Confirm event arrives in the "redwood_private_events" index with those fields mapped to "_time", "request.id", "model.name" respectively.
3) Confirm traces: include the trace_id header (x-trace-id) and an example span for tokenization timing.

Field highlights (from CSV):
- model_name -> model.name (string)
- latency_ms -> event.latency_ms (numeric)
- user_id (hashed) -> user.id (keyword)

Notes on sampling: we recommend sample=1 for the first 24 hours then reduce to 10% for traces.

I'll also upload a pre-filled Splunk HEC token example and a mapping file you can import.

Cheers,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Observability Solutions Engineer
[Attachment: evidence-handshake-checklist-Globex.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@globex.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-09-19T13:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — Splunk HEC integration next steps

Adding the firewall + routing snippets for the staging VPC. Paste these into whichever cloud firewall you use; I included both CIDR-based and hostname allowlists.

Firewall template (example):
- Allow outbound TCP/443 to collector-us-1.redwood-inference.net (we publish DNS -> 52.94.120.0/24).
- Application-level: allow Host: collector-us-1.redwood-inference.net and SNI matching.

If you require egress through a proxy, ensure CONNECT to collector host on port 443 is permitted; we will accept forwarded HEC traffic via proxy without additional config.

Also: for data residency, confirm which regional collector you want (us-east/emea/apac). We'll provision the corresponding hostname and region tag in the mapping file.

Attachment: vpc-firewall-rules-templates.txt

Diego
Diego Fernandez
Network Architect, Redwood Inference
